A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FrameOracle and FrameOracle-41K. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–I support reliable comparison, including matching relocated ablations and renumbered tables.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations, computational measurements, training ablations and human verification of 4,000 dataset instances.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds frame-cost sensitivity, motion-dependent budgeting and larger-input efficiency results.

M1.justification: The cross-modal encoder, Rank Head, K Head, four-stage curriculum and training objectives remain unchanged. The segment-wise inference extension was already present in v2 Appendix F.4 and is retained in v3 Appendix F.3.

E1.justification: The training corpora, FrameOracle-41K, six main benchmarks and appendix MovieChat-1K evaluation are retained. The new motion analysis stratifies existing LongVideoBench data. Newly cited VidHalluc and VideoPASTA are not evaluated.

E2.justification: The comparator sets in Tables 1–2 and the appendix token-budgeting and memory-compression comparisons remain unchanged. Table 3 evaluates the existing LLaVA-Video-7B baseline at additional frame budgets, without introducing another comparison method.

E3.justification: Table 3 adds 32- and 64-frame raw-input settings. Appendix F.4 introduces a six-value frame-cost coefficient sweep, while F.8 groups LongVideoBench videos by adjacent-frame DINOv2 cosine distance and evaluates them with Qwen3-VL-8B. These extend evaluation settings without revising the original protocols.

E4.justification: v3 adds focused analyses of frame-cost sensitivity, motion-dependent frame budgets and raw-frame scaling. Existing curriculum, supervision-backbone, segmentation and ranking-stability analyses are retained. The curriculum ablations appearing as RQ4–6 are relocated from v2 Appendix F.1, not new experiments.

E5.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same significance reporting, including paired question-level bootstrap resampling with 10,000 iterations, 95% confidence intervals and alpha = 0.05. The added analyses introduce no new repeated-run, seed or uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation values are retained. Table 3 adds raw 32/64-frame accuracies of 56.2/56.6 and latencies of 1.140/2.622 seconds. New Table 14 reports sensitivity across coefficient settings; Table 19 reports 24.6/31.0 selected frames and 69.9/68.1 accuracy for low/high motion. These are additional results, not revised same-setting performance.

T1.justification: The selection-policy definitions and objectives in Equations (1)–(3) are unchanged. No theorem, proof, formal assumption or derivation is added or revised; the new analyses are empirical.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements and conclusion retain the same claims about plug-and-play adaptive selection, FrameOracle-41K's novelty and efficiency–accuracy benefits. The headline frame reductions and reported 1.5% accuracy improvement are unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the coefficient sweep as evidence of stability near the default and identifies efficiency or accuracy failures at extreme values. It links larger predicted budgets to greater video motion. Expanded RQ3 also explains the small accuracy gains and substantially higher costs of larger raw-frame inputs.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a project-page URL, and the new analyses document their coefficient settings and motion-score construction. Existing hardware, optimizer, learning rates, batch sizes, training times, data format and prompts remain unchanged. The PDFs alone do not establish what resources the new link provides.

R1.justification: VidHalluc and VideoPASTA citations are added, while Video-LLaVA, VILA and CinePile citations are removed. Several retained references receive publication updates, and Qwen3-VL's blog citation is replaced by its technical report. The main novelty and positioning against prior selection approaches remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 Appendix F.1 is promoted into Section 5.2 as RQ4–6, with reordered questions and light editing. v3 also makes localized wording, author-footnote, conference-header and bibliography-style changes. Most prose and the overall section organization are retained.

P2.justification: Table 3 gains two rows, and new Tables 14 and 19 display the added analyses. v2 Tables 8–10 are relocated and reformatted as v3 Tables 4–6. Figures 1–9, including the appendix qualitative illustrations, remain unchanged; other layout differences mainly reflect text and table reflow.

improvement.justification: v2's efficiency table used only a 16-frame raw baseline; v3 adds 32/64-frame results, making the accuracy–cost trade-off more transparent. New coefficient-sensitivity and motion analyses provide targeted validation, and existing training ablations become easier to find. These are limited evidence and clarity gains; the motion analysis still omits its split threshold and subgroup sizes.
